title: Statistics - Lesson 3: Interquartile Range Practice
description: Quick practice for finding quartiles, calculating IQR, and interpreting the middle 50 percent of data.

questions.question: Which formula gives the interquartile range?
questions.explanation: The interquartile range is the distance from the first quartile to the third quartile, so IQR = Q3 - Q1.

questions.question: A data set has Q1 = 9 and Q3 = 21. What is the IQR? Enter just the number.
Find the IQR of 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14.
questions.explanation: The median is 8. The lower half is 2, 4, 6, so Q1 = 4. The upper half is 10, 12, 14, so Q3 = 12. IQR = 12 - 4 = 8.

questions.question: The IQR measures the spread of the middle 50 percent of a data set.
questions.explanation: Q1 and Q3 mark the boundaries of the middle half, and the IQR measures the distance between them.

questions.question: For 5, 7, 9, 11, 13, which value is left out of both halves when finding Q1 and Q3?
questions.explanation: With an odd number of values, the median is left out of both halves. The median is 9.

questions.question: Find the IQR of 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13, 15. Enter just the number.
questions.explanation: The median is 9. Q1 is 5 and Q3 is 13, so IQR = 13 - 5 = 8.

questions.question: Data Set A has IQR 4. Data Set B has IQR 10. Which statement is best?
options: Data Set A has a more consistent middle 50 percent.
Data Set B has a more consistent middle 50 percent.
Both data sets must have the same maximum.
The data set with IQR 10 has no spread.
questions.explanation: A smaller IQR means the middle half of the data is less spread out.

questions.question: In one sentence, explain why an IQR answer should include context.
questions.correctAnswer: Context tells what the middle 50 percent is measuring, such as scores, minutes, costs, or distances.
questions.explanation: The IQR is a spread, but the interpretation is incomplete unless it says what values are spreading and in what units or situation.
